title: Shader common parameter binding
summary: Recovered shader-common-parameters at VA 0x542230 (261 bytes) as Shader::bindCommonParameters, a genuine i386 thiscall member with no stack arguments. Sixteen ordered stdcall calls to reference helper 0x542340 look up exact names in vertex/pixel constant tables at +0x10/+0x14 and populate handles +0x18..+0x54, assigning shadowMapPos at +0x2c after specularColor at +0x44. Null handles overwrite previous values; lookup failure never short-circuits. Each table field is read again for its call. No reference counting or unrelated field writes occur. Original instructions, original name data and caller 0x5676ce were inspected directly; that caller ignores incidental EAX and returns the object. Both accepted oracle routines and all 228 bytes of test-only name data were checked against immutable Game.exe. Implementation is readable unmatched source, with zero matching-byte credit.
test_description: Fixed-flag GCC i386 freestanding build with Wall/Wextra/Werror passed. Local full differential run passed 430 cases, linking accepted original_shader_common_parameters at 0x542230, original_shader_parameter_lookup at 0x542340 and test-only .oracle_names at 0x9fff74. Test dependency lookupParameter forwards to the actual accepted lookup oracle, not a replacement algorithm. Tests cover all four null-table combinations, table status zero/positive/negative, every constant count 0..16, six missing-handle masks, duplicate reposition names with first or both handles absent, and callbacks changing subsequent table fields to another table or null. Descriptor failure status is intentionally ignored by the original helper. Complete callback logs include object snapshots, checking table selection, enumeration, count reset, call order and intermediate writes against the original. Compare complete guarded objects, immutable prefix, surrounding canaries, final table fields and independently expected handles. Original string data is exact and the recovered requests use portable string literals. A second run without the fixed data mapping passed 16 direct original differential cases (null, empty, failed description, all null handles) and explicitly reported the skipped successful-lookup suite. The local full link requires --section-start=.oracle_common=0x542230 --section-start=.oracle_lookup=0x542340 --section-start=.oracle_names=0x9fff74 after renaming only the two accepted oracle objects' text sections; no instruction modification is performed.
known_limits: lookupParameter is an external stdcall reference dependency, deliberately not recovered within this target. A standalone Linux port must supply it and its constant-table integration; the submitted test adapter calls the accepted original helper directly.

The trusted default link may not place test-only .oracle_names at 0x9fff74. In that configuration test_main explicitly reports only 16 non-string-dereferencing differential cases. The complete 430-case local suite was actually executed with the fixed mapping and passed; no successful-lookup coverage is claimed for an unmapped run.

Only the object prefix through +0x57 is modeled; names/types for the first four DWORDs and the full shader class hierarchy remain unresolved. The observed caller discards EAX; incidental final lookup result in that register is not exposed as a return contract.

Valid object and valid constant-table callback outputs remain original preconditions. Invalid object pointers, malformed descriptors and callbacks throwing or destroying the object are not assigned invented behavior.

MSVC2013-compatible implementation syntax and ABI declarations are provided. The optional /tools/msvc/msvc helper was absent, so native Windows compilation and exact original compiler code generation have not been locally verified. No byte-matching source claim is made.
